answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation, in a company blog statement dated 2026-07-01.
answer.note: NVIDIA says it is introducing a model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure with revenue sharing and credit support: the clouds sell NVIDIA-powered services, while NVIDIA earns standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity. NVIDIA presents this as a potential recurring, usage-linked earnings stream and as a way to expand access to compute as inference and other AI workloads grow. This supports a possible commercial and demand channel for NVIDIA, but does not establish realized revenue or its scale. NVIDIA also says AI clouds are building DSX AI factories; it reports that Firmus is building a Batam campus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs. Those are project statements and expected capacity, not evidence of installed GPUs or NVIDIA orders of that amount. Sharon AI’s CEO separately describes a strategic collaboration with NVIDIA, but the supplied material does not specify its commercial terms.
limitations: The model’s participating counterparties, supported capacity, signing status, revenue-share terms, credit support, and timing are not disclosed; the named Sharon AI and Firmus statements do not establish that either has a specified purchase obligation under this model.
No revenue, order value, margin, or expected contribution to NVIDIA by fiscal period is provided, so the scale and timing of any usage-linked earnings remain unknown.
For the Firmus campus, the statement gives expected scale but no completion schedule, power-delivery status, installed GPU count, or NVIDIA purchase amount.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA filings and earnings disclosures for recognized product revenue, revenue-share income, and any quantified fiscal-year outlook tied to this model.
Check NVIDIA and the named AI clouds’ announcements or filings for counterparties, contract status, supported capacity, commercial terms, and any credit exposure or purchase commitments.
Check Firmus project updates for construction and power milestones, deployment timing, and actual GPU installations or procurement disclosures.
